ncc_locate — 2D matching op

• Data kinds: image → match

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "ncc_locate", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: find_ncc_model (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

*Knob a does not change the output (measured: identical at 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9).*

*Knob b does not change the output (measured: identical at 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9).*

Usage

Finds the best position using template matching based on normalized cross-correlation (NCC). Equivalent to HALCON's find_ncc_model (Find the best matches of an NCC model in an image.).

a, b are unused — the template is not an argument but is pre-registered in the thread-local _MATCH_CTX with set_match_template (the convention shared by the matching ops; see the docstring of _MatchCtx). It computes _ncc_map (the NCC correlation map, [-1,1] by the definition of Lewis 1995) and returns the position of its maximum as [correlation, y, x]. If no template is set, or the input is not a 2-D image, it returns [0,0,0] (no-match) — fail-closed. Rotation and scale changes are not supported (_shape_locate handles rotation).
